title: UK public sector finances, November 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — not a solo morning: it shares the 07:00 minute with Q3 GDP quarterly national accounts and the Q3 balance of payments, the first such stack in six years
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/publicsectorfinancesuknovember2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 42,158 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Public sector finances, UK: November 2026', 'Release date: 22 December 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', and carries the Office for Statistics Regulation accredited-official-statistics statement on the release page itself. Cadence corroborated from the publisher's own JSON bulletin index (api.beta.ons.gov.uk, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200): 137 consecutive PSF bulletins from 2015-04-23 to 2026-08-21 all fall on the 19th-26th, and the eleven November-edition bulletins printed on 2015-12-22, 2016-12-21, 2017-12-21, 2018-12-21, 2019-12-20, 2020-12-22, 2021-12-21, 2022-12-21, 2023-12-21, 2024-12-20 and 2025-12-19. The 07:00 co-print was verified from the same publisher's upcoming-release index: 'GDP quarterly national accounts, UK: July to September 2026' and 'Balance of payments, UK: July to September 2026' are both scheduled 22 December 2026 07:00, each confirmed against its own release page (HTTP 200). Filed estimate on the two counts every ONS entry on this calendar carries: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The date is the publisher's own and is not in doubt
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH OF THIS EVENT, 2026-09-09, after reading both prior proposals (from-uk-cpi-2026-12-16 and from-uk-public-sector-finances-2026-11-20) in full. Both are retitled here on a finding neither had: 07:00 on 2026-12-22 is the ONS quarterly national accounts stack, so PSF publishes the same minute as revised Q3 GDP and the Q3 current account. Measured, that co-print is RARE — 3 of 137 PSF release days since 2015-04-23 (2.2%), last seen 2020-12-22 — and it is also QUIET: QNA release days run IGLT.L 0.77x an ordinary day (t = -1.87) and US 10y 0.75x (t = -2.35), and the three historical co-prints moved IGLT.L 0.580%, 0.253% and 0.321%, all inside the p90 of 0.805%. So it changes the ATTRIBUTION RULE, not the risk: a 07:00 gilt or sterling move on 2026-12-22 belongs to GDP or the current account first and to a monthly borrowing print last. The proposals' shared framing — that this is the LAST outturn on the pre-Budget March 2026 profile — is amended rather than repeated: ONS re-benchmarking is a THREE-STAGE process, and the annual EFO stage lands at the FIRST post-Budget bulletin, not the third (verified in both the 2024-11-21 and 2025-12-19 bulletins, fetched direct). Tiered LOW on this lane's own re-measurement of the 137-day null (IGLT.L 1.07x, t = 0.72; FTSE 0.83x, t = -2.27) and on symbols: [] — this repo tracks no UK-listed name and no house playbook is fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
